title: Vatican II opens, 1962
hook: John XXIII calls a council to bring the Church up to date

segments.voice: Yesterday, Dei Filius, and Vatican One's claim that faith and reason come from one God. Your line was reason reaches toward god. The next council began with a surprise. Day seven hundred ninety.

A new pope, and, the story goes, some expected him simply to keep the seat warm. A small group of cardinals in a Roman basilica, expecting a routine address. And then he tells them he means to call a council for the whole Church. The room, it's said, went quiet. The pope was John the Twenty-third, and the word that came to sum up what he wanted was Italian, his own language: aggiornamento.
screen: `A POPE TO KEEP THE SEAT WARM.` → `A COUNCIL FOR THE WHOLE CHURCH.` → `AGGIORNAMENTO.`

segments.voice: Aggiornamento means bringing up to date. Not replacing, not starting over: updating, the way a family updates an old house it still loves. On the day the council opened, John the Twenty-third gave a speech, known by its first Latin words, Gaudet Mater Ecclesia, Mother Church rejoices. Three things in it are worth carrying. First, he said he disagreed with the prophets of doom, people who could see nothing in the modern world but ruin. He wanted a council that looked at its own age with hope. Second, he drew a distinction that shaped everything after. The ancient teaching of the faith, he said, is one thing; the way it is put into words is another. The substance stays. The way of speaking can change, so that people today can actually hear it. That is aggiornamento in a sentence. Third, he said the Church today would rather use the medicine of mercy than of severity. Now the famous picture. People like to say John the Twenty-third was asked what the council was for, walked to a window and threw it open, to let in fresh air. It's a story people tell. It isn't in the speech, and it may never have happened as told. But it stuck, because it pictured what he'd actually said. The Book of the Apocalypse, in the Douay-Rheims, has God say, "Behold, I make all things new." Not all new things: all things, new. That's today's line: open the windows.
screen: `AGGIORNAMENTO: UP TO DATE.` · `NO PROPHETS OF DOOM.` · `SAME FAITH, NEW WORDS.` · `THE MEDICINE OF MERCY.` · then, large: `OPEN THE WINDOWS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: open a window, literally. If there's one near you, go and open it, even a crack. If not, a door will do, or just turn toward the light. For the sit, stay there. Notice the air coming in: its temperature, its smell, the sounds from outside that weren't in the room a minute ago. Nothing in the room has been thrown out. It's the same room, with air. If you pray, you can let the air carry a prayer for the Church. The bell holds the time.
Aggiornamento. Italian for bringing up to date: the same faith, put into words people today can hear. Today's word.
Your line: open the windows. Today, pick one stale corner of your life, a habit, a grudge, a room, and let some air in, without throwing out what you love. Day seven hundred ninety.

howItsDone: Catholics remember the Second Vatican Council through its documents, read in parishes and schools, and the word aggiornamento is still used when describing how the Church presents its unchanging faith to each new age.

fork.setup: you're a pope opening a council. some advisers see only ruin in the modern world. what do you tell the bishops?
options: agree, and call the council to condemn the age.
disagree with the prophets of doom, and choose mercy.
postpone the council until times improve.
fork.reveal: John XXIII said he disagreed with the prophets of doom and that the Church would rather use the medicine of mercy than severity.

original.note: Italian, bringing up to date; the word became shorthand for John XXIII's hope for the council.
